items.title: Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 Hard Mode Is No Joke — Watch AI-Controlled Orks Wipe the Floor With 2 Developers Playing Space Marines
items.excerpt: When developers show off their games, they tend to defeat the enemy AI in spectacular fashion. But that’s exactly the opposite of what happens in the gameplay King Art Games just released for its upcoming real-time strategy game Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4.
items.content_text: When developers show off their games, they tend to defeat the enemy AI in spectacular fashion. But that’s exactly the opposite of what happens in the gameplay King Art Games just released for its upcoming real-time strategy game Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 . In the video, below, creative director Jan Theysen and senior game designer Elliott Verbiest team up against Hard AI Orks in a 2v2 Team Skirmish PvE battle. These two developers have been at the helm of pretty much all the Dawn of War 4 battlefield report videos released so far. But those previous gameplay videos focus on PvP; this time, Theysen and Verbiest join forces to face the enemy AI — and they decide to go up against hard mode. The video shows two matches, the first of which goes so spectacularly badly for the poor developers that they suffer defeat in just over four minutes. They declare that a practice round — mere training before the second match, in which the pair promise they're “locked in.” They also increase the number of Victory Points needed to help extend the length of the match... just in case. Well, that didn’t help either. The brutal, overwhelming Orks stomp all over the Emperor’s finest, delivering the kind of sweeping beatdown befitting of a Waaagh! Theysen and Verbiest do their best to keep pace with capturing points and objectives, but are unable to fend off wave after wave of attacks even with auto reinforce of their units on. Behind in Victory Points and starved of resources, Theysen and Verbiest have to way to generate a response army to fight back when the Orks make a push towards their base. “I think I have to have a stern word with our coders about the hard mode difficulty,” Theysen jokes as he realises the Space Marines are done for. “I mean it’s supposed to be hard but also the boss is supposed to win!” “I have no doubt that players will come back to us within like a few weeks of launch and tell us, ‘Actually we've managed to beat this within two days,’ Verbiest adds. “I’m pretty sure that the people in the comments will discuss our shortcomings!” Theysen concludes. This second match and the video itself ends unceremoniously: with Theysen hitting the surrender button before the Orks deliver the final blow. “This might be the second loss in a row which tells you two things,” he says. “First of all, we are not that good at our own game. And also the AI is pretty strong. “This is a surrender. It was an honor playing with you, but we didn't make it. Maybe next time. See you soon. Bye.” And that’s that. The second match lasted 13 minutes, which is a lot better than the first, but clearly not what Theysen and Verbiest were hoping for. I actually really enjoyed the video, not only because it offers a first look at two-player co-op against the enemy AI, but because it shows how confident the developers are in the game itself. They could have thrown that gameplay out and recorded a new match on normal difficulty, or even tried hard AI again, and again, until they secured a win. But no, they wanted fans to see what Dawn of War 4 looks like as it stands today — warts and all — even if that means the developers aren’t covered in glory in the process. It seems fans have responded well to the video too. “Pretty cool that you guys showed the defeat and how hard the AI can be. Quite interesting!” one person said in the YouTube comments. “I will never do hard in a Warhammer game Orks just nuke you,” another person, clearly familiar with the way Orks work, offered. Dawn of War 4 hits PC on December 3, 2026. I think I’m going to stick with normal difficulty!
items.title_en: Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 Hard Mode Is No Joke — Watch AI-Controlled Orks Wipe the Floor With 2 Developers Playing Space Marines

items.content_text: Just a week after the Steam Frame presented Valve's vision for VR gaming, Meta is getting ready to take the stage at Meta Connect 2026. items.title: Producer of Zach Cregger's Resident Evil Movie Reportedly Working on New Silent Hill Film
items.excerpt: A new report from The Wall Street Journal states that Roy Lee, who produced Zach Cregger’s hugely-successful Resident Evil movie, is now working on a Silent Hill film.
items.content_text: A new report from The Wall Street Journal states that Roy Lee, who produced Zach Cregger’s hugely-successful Resident Evil movie, is now working on a Silent Hill film. Roy Lee is a Hollywood legend. The producer has had a hand in some of the most successful movies of the last three decades and has a speciality for adapting pre-existing IP, specifically where horror is concerned. He began his career with horror hits like The Grudge and The Ring, and went on to produce Zach Cregger’s Barbarian and Weapons 20 years later. Most recently, he helped bring Cregger’s Resident Evil to life, which has become the single most-successful film adaptation of Capcom’s video game series ever and the highest-rated video game movie of all time. Now, it seems that he’s working on yet another iconic survival horror franchise: Silent Hill. The Wall Street Journal published a feature about Roy Lee on September 20, where the outlet shed some light on the producer’s upcoming video game-related projects. According to the article, Lee has a staggering 20 or so movies and television adaptations for video games that are in development or production right now. These include Prime Video’s God of War series , Michael B. Jordan’s Battlefield movie , and, most curiously, “Japanese horror classic Silent Hill.” The existence of a new Silent Hill movie has not been publicly confirmed at the time of writing this article; however, Konami has been extremely bullish on the franchise as of late, releasing two Silent Hill games in as many years, both of which have been well-received. Silent Hill producer Motoi Okamoto also revealed that Konami hopes to release a new game in the series every year as it works to reinvigorate its IPs across the board, including titles like Castlevania. With this in mind, the fact that another Silent Hill movie is getting made so soon after the release of Return to Silent Hill isn’t too surprising… especially given the success of Cregger’s Resident Evil. Return to Silent Hill , however, was a flop. It’s safe to say that hardcore fans of the franchise hated it, and critics’ opinions weren’t much better. We at IGN scored the movie a five out of 10 , saying in our review that it “isn’t the worst entry in this video game movie series, but it fails to accomplish anything that the source material doesn’t do better.” For now, fans can remain cautiously optimistic for a better take on Silent Hill now that Lee is reportedly bringing his expertise to the project... though Resident Evil fans have been somewhat divided as to how Cregger handled the source material in his latest movie, particularly its ending .
items.title_en: Producer of Zach Cregger's Resident Evil Movie Reportedly Working on New Silent Hill Film

items.title: Robert Pattinson Reacts to Fans Asking for Him to Play the Joker After Primetime Performance Goes Viral
items.excerpt: Robert Pattinson’s captivating performance as Chris Hansen in A24’s Primetime has sparked an unexpected trend; fans are now wondering what Pattinson’s take on the Joker would look like.
items.content_text: Robert Pattinson’s captivating performance as Chris Hansen in A24’s Primetime has sparked an unexpected trend; fans are now wondering what Pattinson’s take on the Joker would look like. The actor’s portrayal of Hansen has received acclaim from both critics and casual audiences alike. IGN’s Siddhant Adlakha scored Primetime a sparkling 9 out of 10 , praising Pattinson for “setting the screen ablaze” with his depiction of a “petulant, paranoid” TV host. One of his lines from the movie’s trailers has already become a viral meme (“You see how this looks, right?”), and fans just can’t get enough of his chilling stare and near-sociopathic take on Hansen, prompting them to ask the question: “What if he played the Joker?” In the lead-up to Primetime’s release on September 25, curious Batman fans are hypothetically casting him in James Gunn’s separate DC cinematic universe, wondering what his Hansen-esque Joker would look like, were he able and willing to play the part. “Really sucks he’s Batman, ‘cause his Joker would’ve been generational,” one fan wrote in a post on X. “F**k it, let Robert Pattinson play Joker and Batman,” another said , while another mused that the “only bad part about Robert Pattinson being such a good Batman is that he’d make such a good Joker.” Really sucks he’s Batman cause his Joker would’ve been generational https://t.co/6fHhzKUFGw — woop (@woop54) September 16, 2026 Entertainment Weekly brought up these remarks to Pattinson during a September 2026 interview, who humbly deferred to Barry Keoghan, who’s currently playing the villain in Matt Reeves’ film series. “Oh, Jesus. I mean, it’s such a great part… but Barry’s the man,” Pattinson told the outlet. He went on to praise Keoghan’s performance as the iconic DC character, pointing specifically to their shared deleted scene in 2022’s The Batman . “I loved doing that scene with him so much,” he admitted. “I love Barry, as well. I think he’s such a phenomenal actor. It was so fun doing that stuff with him. But yeah, I want him to do it. I’m much more interested in that.” Battinson is set to return to the screen in February 2028. Filming is already underway, with fans in Scotland posting photos from the film’s set showing the Batmobile fleeing from Gotham police. Photos hinting at an upgraded batsuit have also been shared online, sparking even more speculation as to what will happen to Bruce Wayne in his next highly-anticipated adventure on the silver screen. For now, all we know for sure is that Pattinson's next Batman movie will go in a "totally different direction," as told by the actor in an interview earlier this month.

items.title: The Conjuring Gets Its First-Ever Video Game Coming to Netflix Next Month
items.excerpt: The Conjuring is coming to Netflix in the form of a video game, marking the franchise’s first foray into the medium after releasing ten films over the last decade.
items.content_text: The Conjuring is coming to Netflix in the form of a video game, marking the franchise’s first foray into the medium after releasing ten films over the last decade. Titled The Conjuring: Unspoken, the game is slated to launch on the streamer this October. As spotted by Polygon , this news was announced unceremoniously in the platform’s monthly New on Netflix newsletter, which had only a small blurb to share about what players can expect from this latest entry in Ed and Lorraine Warren’s ghostly adventures. “What is haunting the Red Lion Inn? Scan for paranormal signals and investigate the eerie events troubling a grieving family in this cinematic game,” the blurb reads. Thus far, anything else about the game is unknown; we aren’t sure if it’ll mimic Netflix’s most recent horror game, Unhinged , which was a first-person, interactive title featuring a celebrity cast including Zoë Kravitz and Sadie Sink, or if it’ll be something completely different. We don’t even know if Ed or Lorraine will be in the game at all, though it would seem odd if they weren’t, as the blurb makes it seem like the pair is going off on one of their iconic paranormal investigations again. What we do know is that, unlike other games under Netflix’s umbrella, it’ll be a cloud-based title, presumably not tied to mobile devices or any particular platform. It's also cinematic, meaning that it'll almost certainly contain grand cutscenes and a heavy narrative focus. This marks The Conjuring’s very first fully-dedicated video game adaptation, and it’s coming right in time for spooky season. While an exact launch date has not yet been shared, it’ll release on the heels of Silent Hill: Townfall , the second title from Konami’s horror series that’s released in the last two years. It’s received rave reviews thus far, with IGN scoring the game an 8 out of 10 — so it looks like Untold has its work cut out for it if it hopes to catch players’ attention. The Conjuring has been featured in another game, though; Fortnite notably included a map themed after The Conjuring: Last Rites , in 2025. Last Rites is the newest film in the famous horror series first kicked off by James Wan in 2013, and the final story in ‘phase one’ of its overarching narrative. Another installment is releasing in 2027 titled The Conjuring: First Communion, though details on this movie are also slim at the moment. Cloud-based gaming is a big focus for Netflix at the moment, thanks to the success of Unhinged this summer. “We're scratching the surface in terms of what we think the total potential of the space offers for us,” co-CEO Greg Peters told investors in a July 2026 call . “You're going to see us continue to calibrate and refine our level of investment here, which is still very small relative to our overall content spend based on demonstrated performance based on what is working for our members and what's delivering returns to our business.” We just hope that the studio making The Conjuring: Untold doesn’t get shuttered like Unhinged’s developer, Nightschool, did, despite being responsible for one of the steamer’s “most successful cloud game debuts” ever.
items.title_en: The Conjuring Gets Its First-Ever Video Game Coming to Netflix Next Month

items.title: The Grond LEGO Set Is Free When You Buy LEGO Lord of the Rings Minas Tirith
items.excerpt: LEGO has brought back the Grond battering ram set as a free Gift with Purchase when you buy the massive LEGO Lord of the Rings Minas Tirith.
items.content_text: It’s back. LEGO has brought back LEGO Lord of the Rings Grond , a 307-piece set based on the wolf-shaped battering ram the Orcs use to shatter the Great Gate of Minas Tirith in the Battle of the Pelennor Fields. It’s an awesome-looking set, and between now and September 30 it’s free – in a manner of speaking. There’s only one catch: to get it, you have to buy the $650 LEGO Minas Tirith set from the LEGO Store . I’m sorry. Get Grond Free with LEGO The Lord of the Rings: Minas Tirith Grond is what LEGO calls a Gift with Purchase” or “GWP.” These are smaller free sets LEGO gives you When you buy select sets from the official LEGO Store . GWPs are limited edition, and are not available to purchase separately. The problem is, they’re only available for a limited time, and LEGO often runs out of stock before that time is up. Sometimes, however, LEGO brings them back. That’s the case with Grond. The Grond set is available once again, while supplies last, as a Minas Tirith GWP until September 30. As is fitting for any GWP accompanying the mammoth Minas Tirith set, Grond isn’t actually all that small. Valued at $29.99, it has you build a rolling support structure as well as the beastly, flame-throwing battering ram. It also includes two weapon-wielding Orc minifigures. Minas Tirith, meanwhile, is a 8,278-piece behemoth, the largest LEGO Lord of the Rings set ever released. Kevin Wong , our go-to LEGO expert, built this gorgeous set and wrote about the experience, concluding, “It receives our highest recommendation.” If you do buy the pricy Minas Tirith set, you’ll also get another GWP set in addition to Grond. That’s LEGO Scary Haunted Tree (which comes with all orders of $100 or more). If you enter an exclusive code found over on The Brick Fan at checkout, you might even be able to get LEGO Ideas Friendly Snails for free as well. For more, check out our running list of every upcoming LEGO set announced so far.

items.title: Game of Thrones Star Kit Harington Isn't a Gamer, but He's Excited for Grand Theft Auto 6
items.excerpt: Game of Thrones star Kit Harington has confessed that he isn't much of a gamer, but wants to play Grand Theft Auto 6.
items.content_text: Game of Thrones star Kit Harington has confessed that he isn't much of a gamer, but wants to play Grand Theft Auto 6 . The actor best known for playing Jon Snow reflected on his experience with the gaming world with Josh Horowitz in a recent interview . After recalling his experience working on Silent Hill: Revelation, a live-action film based on the beloved horror gaming franchise, he was asked if he was much of a gamer. Harington noted he didn't have much experience with the Silent Hill games, but played a bit of Tekken, Mario Kart, Diddy Kong Racing, and most recently, Hogwarts Legacy. When Horowitz asked if he'd ever dabbled in Grand Theft Auto, Harington said that he wants to play Grand Theft Auto 6 after seeing some of the advertising. He went on to express an admiration for videos that mimic GTA's tropes in real life. All of this sort of goes to show that the GTA 6 effect is beginning to happen, as even non-gamers are getting pulled in by its trance. Rockstar is spending a boatload of cash to get the game in front of as many people as possible. It has assembled an Avengers-level ensemble of musicians to craft an original soundtrack for Grand Theft Auto 6, spent nearly $1 million on a "Welcome to Vice City" sign in Miami , and is likely only going to continue to ramp things up as we get closer to launch. NBA star Steven Adams also joked that he expects the performance of the league to drop when GTA 6 releases in November. As for Harington specifically, he didn't say whether or not he will actually end up playing GTA 6 or not. He's had some experience in the gaming world, as he was the main antagonist in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare and voiced Jon Snow in Telltale's Game of Thrones video game. His next big role will be playing Gildroy Lockhart in HBO's Harry Potter TV series, which may explain why he recently dabbled in Hogwarts Legacy. Photo by Kristina Bumphrey/Variety via Getty Images

items.title: Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls PC Sales Figures and Player Count Spark Worry From Players About Game's Longevity
items.excerpt: It’s been over a month since Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls released, and its early sales figures and player counts on PC are sparking concern within the fighting game community about its longevity.
items.content_text: It’s been over a month since Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls released, and its early sales figures and player counts on PC are sparking concern within the fighting game community about its longevity. Arc System Works’ latest tag fighting game has suffered no end of discourse within the FGC; some players love it, while others are severely dissatisfied with its tag system and online matchmaking, and it’s almost impossible to avoid this debate if you’re on fighting game Twitter right now. Most everyone was excited for a new, fast-paced Marvel fighting game from the developers of the highly-lauded Guilty Gear series and Dragon Ball FighterZ — but after launch, that excitement seems to have dwindled into a spiral of frustration. Data from Steam Charts shows that the title boasts a current active PC player count of 427 players on Steam, with a 24-hour peak of 791 players. The game’s all-time peak on Steam is listed at 13,787 players, but keep in mind that these are just Steam figures and don’t account for PlayStation users. Sales figures for Tokon on PC have also driven discourse around the game; data from Alinea Analytics shows a cavernous disparity between platforms, with 82% of copies being sold on PlayStation compared to just 18% on Steam. That being said, it has generated an estimated $49.7 million in revenue, selling approximately 750,000 copies across both platforms combined. Those numbers aren’t anything to sniff at, and it’s worth noting that the competition is stiff. Street Fighter 6 is definitely the most successful fighting game on the market right now, and Tokon was unlikely to ever topple it. The game is certainly seeing success on PlayStation — but its extremely rough launch on PC is likely to blame for the severe disparity between who's playing on what platform. The game infamously suffered issues with its PC port at launch, to the point where prominent community figure Maximilian Dood literally uninstalled it during one of his live streams in a damning moment that went viral. While a patch was quickly released to help solve these problems, Tokon’s producer admitted that it would be difficult to regain players’ trust after this, and the game’s director, Kazuto Sekine, apologized for the ordeal in an honest statement a month later. While Tokon appears to be thriving on PlayStation, its comparatively lackluster playerbase on PC and strikingly smaller sales figures on Steam have sparked a debate within the fighting game community as to whether or not the game has what it takes to weather the storm in an increasingly crowded market of IP-based tag fighting games (hello, Invincible VS and Avatar Legends). We also can’t discount the fact that the game was initially blocked in 132 countries due to PSN requirements. One of the loudest voices in this conversation is Guilty Gear and Smash Bros pro William ‘Leffen’ Hjelte. “Unless Tokon turns the game around gameplay wise by next patch, I'm gonna drop it,” he wrote in a viral post on X/Twitter. “Gameplay aside, I can't even get matches in EU, it feels like the serious playerbase is maybe, at best, 1/10th of Strive’s and 2XKO’s here. “I genuinely think the game is saveable if they act fast and correctly, but with us not even knowing when the patch is coming and only four characters coming (no date), I think it's probably over, at least if you care about having a big scene. Very sad, I had a lot of high hopes for Tokon.” I genuinely think the game is saveable if they act fast and correctly but with us not even knowing when the patch is coming and only 4 chars coming (no date) I think its probably over, at least if you care about having a big scene. Very sad, I had a lot of high hopes for Tokon. — Leffen (@TSM_Leffen) September 22, 2026 “Dragon Ball FighterZ sold over two million copies in its first week,” another player pointed out. “Tokon probably won't even break one million in six months. This is truly sad that they fumbled such an easy win.” “Yeah... This game will only have a year's worth of content, and only because it's already made or in the planning stages. I don't think Cyclops will bring in the crowd Tokon needs,” another speculated . Others, however, are arguing that it’s only been just under two months since the game came out, and are pointing to its success on PlayStation as to why things might not be as grim as some voices in the FGC believe. “Marvel Tokon came out August 6. Not even two months ago,” YouTuber and prominent community member Mightykeef said. “Not… even… two months ago. I’ve seen such an insane amount of doom posting for a fighting game that has not even been able to breath for two months, lol.” “Tokon is an incredible fighting game, but it's still a fighting game. Always a niche genre. Hell, one of the goats of the genre, UMVC3, didn't crack 600k in two months,” another pointed out . “It took Marvel vs Capcom 2 years to become the mythical legend it is. Started in arcade, then ported over to Dreamcast, PS2, Xbox. It’s not gonna happen overnight. And I love Tokon, I want more of it. We need to really end the stupid seasonal DLC crap. Just launch with more characters,” another said. The FGC culture is so different than I remember. Marvel Tokon came out August 6th. Not even two months ago. Not… even… two months ago. I’ve seen such an insane amount of doom posting for a fighting game that has not even been able to breath for two months lol https://t.co/1LGW70FoEG — Mightykeef (@MightyKeef) September 23, 2026 What’s your take on this conversation? Do you think Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is in a healthy state with a bright future ahead, or do you believe that the game is already on its way to irrelevance? Let us know in the comments below.

items.title: Crocodile Dundee Is Getting a 4K Steelbook Edition for Its 40th Anniversary
items.excerpt: Crocodile Dundee, the 1980s blockbuster hit, is getting the 4K steelbook treatment in honor of its 40th anniversary.
items.content_text: Crocodile Dundee, the 1986 box office hit, is getting the 4K steelbook treatment. The movie will be available December 1 for $39.99, but it’s available now for preorder at Amazon . I, for one, am excited. It may be hard to imagine now, in an era when theatrical releases for comedies are few and far between, but there was a period during the 1980s when Crocodile Dundee was king. The character, played by Paul Hogan, was a pop culture icon. That’s because this movie was a mega-hit. Crocodile Dundee - 4K Steelbook Edition Made for under $10 million, Crocodile Dundee grossed $328 million worldwide, landing it at number two on the list of highest-grossing movies of 1986, behind only Top Gun . That’s a remarkable feat for a movie about an Outback outdoorsman. Crocodile Dundee works because it’s a mix of tried-and-true ideas: It’s a fish-out-of-water story and a romance between an unlikely couple. It starts when Sue Charlton (Linda Kozlowski), a New York journalist, travels to the Australian Outback and meets the titular hero, a hunter who feels more at home in the wilderness than he does around other people. Soon Sue invites Croc to come back to NYC with her. He agrees, and plenty of comedic hijinks ensue as Dundee’s outdoorsy sensibilities clash with city living. Cue Sue’s gradual romantic feelings toward Dundee, and her ambivalence about her current boyfriend. The movie spawned a less-revered sequel in 1988, followed over a decade later by 2001’s Crocodile Dundee in Los Angeles. items.title: 4 Burning Doomsday Questions We Have After Avengers: Endgame Encore
items.excerpt: The new scenes from Avengers: Endgame Encore have leaked online, and they raise some very interesting questions about the plot of Avengers: Doomsday. Let's break it all down.
items.content_text: Marvel is about to release Avengers: Endgame Encore in theaters. Not only is this a chance to rewatch the climax of the Infinity Saga on the big screen again, it also gives fans several new scenes to chew on. Each of these scenes is meant to create connective tissue with Avengers: Doomsday and lay the groundwork for the debut of Robert Downey, Jr.’s Doctor Doom. Those scenes have now leaked onto the Internet ahead of Endgame Encore’s release [Note - we’re pretty confident these leaks are genuine, but you can never be 100% sure in the age of AI.]. And there’s definitely a lot of food for thought here. We see key TVA figures reacting to the impending collapse of the multiverse and Doom himself kicking off some sort of recruiting spree. These scenes raise more questions than they answer about the plot of Doomsday, so let’s break down what we do and don’t know right now. What Does Doom Want With Hulk? In what is easily the most intriguing new addition to Endgame, we get a scene focused on Mark Ruffalo’s Bruce Banner set in the aftermath of Spider-Man: Brand New Day. Banner has clearly seen better days, as he’s still recovering from the physical and psychological trauma of being hijacked by Sadie Sink’s Jean Grey . He’s desperate to reassert control over his Hulk persona, and so he’s locked himself deep in an underground bunker to test a new “gamma suppression system.” But no sooner does Banner begin his test than the lights flicker and a certain armored villain makes his presence known. We hear (but don’t see) Downey’s Doom, who proclaims “I’ve come to collect you.” Both men then vanish, leaving only a glowing green rune on the ground (similar to the ones left when Asgardians travel on the Rainbow Bridge). So the obvious question here is what Doom wants with Banner. He seems to be building some sort of team, but to what end? Is he more interested in Banner’s brains or Hulk’s brawn? We’d guess the former, as past movies have already set up the character as a voice of authority in the growing multiverse crisis. And judging from the Doomsday trailers and the fact that Doom can deflect Thor’s mighty Stormbreaker with ease, we doubt he’s in need of any extra muscle. Is Doom assembling his own team of Avengers here? If so, what other characters might he be recruiting? Is it possible he’s building a version of the Illuminati as a brain trust to deal with Incursions? In the lead-up to the 2015 Secret Wars comic, the Illuminati also included members like Iron Man, Mister Fantastic, Beast, Namor, Black Panther, and Black Bolt. Doom himself wasn’t a member of that team, but he was working toward similar goals and forged his own alliances. Will the MCU Doom seek these heroes out on Earth-616? Or is Doom planning for a post-multiverse future here? We have to wonder if Downey’s character has already given up on saving reality as it currently exists and is building his Battleworld contingency plan. Perhaps he wants Banner to serve as one of the barons on Battleworld (a role that a version of Hulk did fill in the comic). Whatever the case, it seems that Ruffalo has a bigger part to play in Avengers: Doomsday than we realized. Ruffalo wasn’t even part of the initial cast chair announcement . But if there’s one takeaway from Avengers: Endgame Encore, it’s that Doomsday’s cast is going to be even bigger than we thought. Why Is the Multiverse Collapsing? Another new scene shows us the current state of things at the TVA, as Mr. Mobius (Owen Wilson), Casey (Eugene Cordero), and Ouroboros (Ke Huy Quan) confront the rapidly deteriorating situation with the multiverse. They can only watch their charmingly low-res computer displays as worlds begin colliding and some Earths declare all-out war on each other. By the end of the scene, it’s reported that no fewer than 3000 Incursions are happening simultaneously. One of those looks to be Earth-10005, the home of Fox’s X-Men. This scene makes it clear that, even with Marvel pivoting away from Jonathan Majors’ Kang the Conqueror as the central villain of the Multiverse Saga, the Loki series is going to be an important precursor to Doomsday. That series chronicled the rebirth of the multiverse and placed Tom Hiddleston’s redeemed Loki at the heart of creation . But no sooner has the multiverse been restored than it’s started to come apart at the seams. Why is that, exactly? What’s the root cause of the multiverse’s collapse and the threat of Incursions? Why does it seem to be happening all at once rather than gradually? Is this why Doom is suddenly making his presence known on Earth-616? This scene may hold an important clue. Early on, we hear TVA mascot Miss Minutes (Tara Strong) reminding her employees that it’s essential for all beings to remain within their home universes for the sake of existence. Unfortunately, there’s one pivotal character who doesn’t seem to have followed the rules. What Is Loki Doing at Steve and Peggy’s House? Endgame Encore puts the heartwarming ending of the original Endgame in a very different context. This time, the film lingers longer with the dancing Steve Rogers (Chris Evans) and Peggy Carter (Hayley Atwell), as a tender kiss is interrupted by a knock at the door. Steve quickly hides while Peggy answers, only to realize the person at the door is none other than Loki. We can infer from Loki’s TVA attire that this is a version of the character from sometime in the middle of the Loki series. He’s committed to the TVA’s mission, but hasn’t yet taken his place atop the multiversal throne. And echoing Miss Minutes’ warning broadcast, we can only assume that Loki has come to tell Steve that he’s violating the laws of existence by travelling back in time to be with Peggy. That said, we don’t think Loki is there to force Steve to return to his rightful place and time. Obviously, Steve has remained MIA in the present-day MCU ever since journeying back in time with the Infinity Stones. And we know from the very first Doomsday trailer that Steve and Peggy remain together long enough to raise a baby together. By the time Steve does reunite with the Avengers in Doomsday, he’s clearly older and sporting his beard again. So what exactly is Loki’s intention here? Has he found some loophole that will allow Steve to remain in the past with Peggy? If so, why is he so committed to letting one man violate the basic laws of the TVA? Is it just his way of thanking Steve for helping to restore the lives Thanos took? Most importantly, does this mean Captain America is the catalyst causing all these Incursions? Given Miss Minutes’ ominous warning, we have to assume that Steve’s decision to do something for himself for a change has cost the multiverse dearly. What Is the Significance of Doom’s Armor? Avengers: Endgame Encore wraps with one final addition to the original film. Endgame originally had no post-credits scenes (a rarity for the MCU, to be sure). All it had to offer fans who stuck around through the credits was the sound of a hammer striking metal, a callback to Downey’s Tony Stark forging his original suit of armor in 2008’s Iron Man. But here again, Encore presents this ending in a very different context. This version ends with that same sound, but this time we see Doom forging his metal mask. It’s a fun way of subverting the original Endgame, and it almost tricks you into believing that introducing Doom was the plan way back in 2019. Apart from ending Encore on a fitting note, this scene does highlight one particular question. What is the actual significance of Doom’s armor? Why is he wearing it in the first place? We can see from the trailers and the aforementioned Hulk scene that Doom is gifted with immense magical abilities, so why is it so important that he also be decked out in a technologically advanced suit? In the comics, of course, Doom used the armor to hide his scarred face. Is he masking similar injuries here? Based on one of the Doomsday posters and Vanessa Kirby’s dialogue in the second trailer , we’re assuming Doom is also mourning the deaths of his family. Does the armor somehow tie back to that tragedy? The presence of a sash on his left arm (a relic of his late wife?) certainly seems to suggest so. Answers to these questions will have to wait until Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters on December 18. Until then, let us know your theories about the new Avengers: Endgame Encore footage in the comments below. Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky .
items.title_en: 4 Burning Doomsday Questions We Have After Avengers: Endgame Encore

items.content_text: If you're a Tolkien fan, you likely know that there's always more lore to discover. That's where the Silmarillion comes in. Unlike the other Lord of the Rings books that focus on narrative storytelling, the Silmarillion is a deep dive into the mythology and history that defines Middle Earth. It's an essential look into the fantasy world J.R.R. Tolkien so lovingly created. The Silmarillion is available in multiple versions, but the illustrated editions offer the best overall experience thanks to maps, drawings, and more from Tolkien himself. If you're interested in learning more about Middle Earth straight from the source, Amazon is currently discounting the collector's edition to its lowest price ever ahead of Prime Big Deal Days . Note : This is a Prime-exclusive deal, so you will need to have an active Amazon Prime Membership to get the discount. If you're not already familiar with what the Silmarillion actually is, here's a quick rundown: This book covers the early history of its fictional universe, Eä, and the various lands it contains. This includes Valinor, Beleriand, Númenor, and, of course, Middle-Earth. Broken up into five distinct parts, readers can expect deep lore exposition, extensive historical accounts of the First Age, and summaries of the Third Age stories we know and love, the Lord of the Rings. The illustrated edition itself is 432 pages long and includes the complete text of the Silmarillion alongside full-color prints of Tolkien's illustrations. It also includes two removable fold-out maps. It's essentially a deep dive into the inner workings of one of the best-selling fantasy franchises of all time. items.title: GTA 6 Shirts Given Away for Free at Tokyo Game Show Are Being Resold Online for Hundreds of Dollars
items.excerpt: GTA 6 shirts that were given away for free exclusively at Tokyo Game Show 2026 are already being resold online for hundreds of dollars.
items.content_text: GTA 6 shirts that were given away for free exclusively at Tokyo Game Show 2026 are already being resold online for hundreds of dollars. Attendees at Tokyo Game Show who got the chance to participate in a special immersive screening for GTA 6’s viral Netflix special were treated to commemorative T-shirts to celebrate the occasion. This screening was the exact same extended trailer that launched on Netflix last month, but with more bells and whistles; it featured tricks like surround sound and 4D haptic effects that correlated with what was happening on screen, letting viewers feel like they were actually tagging along with Jason and Lucia as they fled from the fuzz and held up corner stores. The experience was so popular that the GTA 6 booth closed after just 10 minutes , having already reached capacity — but savvy fans saw an opportunity to capitalize on the overwhelming demand and make some quick cash. As spotted by Dexerto , the commemorative T-shirts handed out by PlayStation at the game's TGS 2026 booth for free have already made their way online and are being resold on platforms like eBay for hundreds of dollars. A quick browse on eBay shows a handful of listings pricing the shirts around $140 - $200, while other goodies that were given out at Rockstar’s booth, like GTA 6-branded stickers and carabiners , are being marked up to the tune of $30 - $40. This isn’t a new phenomenon, by far; exclusive merchandise like this has become a target for scalpers across several big franchises over the last few years. One Piece’s viral collaboration with Popeye’s is a prime example of this, as scalpers waited in lines that trailed blocks away from their local fast food franchises to snag special Luffy-themed bento boxes, only to list them online for staggeringly high prices. The same can be said of the Pokemon Trading Card scene; scalpers have become ravenous for Pokemon card packs and merchandise, causing chaos at retailers and even sparking violent confrontations that have ended in arrests. The hype for GTA 6 is at an all-time high, so we can’t say that these shirts getting resold online is a huge surprise. The city of Miami is even working with Rockstar on some special advertising for the game, having recently erected a massive, $1 million 'Welcome to Vice City' sign after entering talks with officials for a possible GTA 6-themed takeover of the entire area .

items.title: How to Watch Dragon Ball in Order: Series, Sagas, and Movies
items.excerpt: From the mind of the legendary Akira Toriyama, the Dragon Ball timeline includes seven anime series and over twenty movies and specials. Here's how to watch it all in order.
items.content_text: It's easy to underestimate just how influential the Dragon Ball franchise is, but the Akira Toriyama manga essentially defined what an action shonen manga would be for the next 40 years. Goku became the archetypical anime protagonist , while his relationship with Vegeta became the standard that all anime rivalries would emulate. It helped popularize power-up transformations, time jumps, and much more in both anime and manga. Sure, it's easy to boil down Dragon Ball to just having extremely long fight scenes, but the franchise is much more than that. With bold changes in tone, from hilarious gag comedy to meaningful moments of inspiration, as well as a myriad of great side characters, Dragon Ball remains as good as its reputation would suggest. Still, this is one of the longest-running anime franchises, with dozens of movies in addition to several anime series. It can be hard to navigate the Dragon Ball universe, but that's what this guide is for. Whether you fell off the wagon at one point and want to catch up, or you're looking to embark on your very first journey with Son Goku, here's how to watch every Dragon Ball anime and movie in order. How Long Is the Dragon Ball Anime? Inspired by Akira Toriyama's manga of the same name, Dragon Ball includes over 800 episodes across five anime series. There have also been over 20 anime movies set in the Dragon Ball universe, which expand the story or even continue it. Now, what about canon? That's where it gets a bit complicated. Granted, Toriyama never really cared much about canon, as he constantly tinkered with his story, retconning things whenever he thought of something better than he had before (remember when Goku was just a happy monkey guy and not an alien superhero?). Still, what makes Dragon Ball canon complicated is that while most of the movies aren't technically canon, the last four movies are part of the official Dragon Ball continuity. Then there's Dragon Ball Daima , a canon anime series that seemed to make Dragon Ball GT , a show long considered to be non-canon, somewhat canon. So what does this mean? Well, it is kind of up to the audience. If you like Dragon Ball GT, then you can think of it as canon. If you prefer to skip it, then by all means, do so. Where to Watch Dragon Ball The full scope of everything Dragon Ball is on Crunchyroll . The anime streaming service is also the only place you'll find most of the movies, though Z Kai and Daima are also streaming on Hulu. For the collectors, all of the Dragon Ball series and movies are available as physical releases. How to Watch Dragon Ball in Order 1. Dragon Ball (Episodes 1-13) Pilaf Saga 2. Dragon Ball: Curse of the Blood Rubies (Movie) An alternate retelling of the first saga of the story. Best watched after the Emperor Pilaf Saga rather than have this be your first exposure to the characters. 3. Dragon Ball (Episode 14) Start of Tournament Saga 4. Dragon Ball: Sleeping Princess in Devil's Castle (Movie) Goku and Krillin are tasked to save a sleeping princess from Lucifer (yes, that Lucifer). The movie takes place at the start of Goku and Krillin's training. 5. Dragon Ball (Episodes 15-28) Finish Tournament Saga 6. Dragon Ball: Mystical Adventure (Movie) Goku and Krillin join the World Martial Arts Tournament while Bora hides a Dragon Ball from the emperor's evil forces. 7. Dragon Ball: The Path to Power (Movie) An alternate retelling of the story so far, merging the first two sagas with some cool changes. 8. Dragon Ball (Episodes 29-153) Red Ribbon Army Saga General Blue Saga Commander Red Saga Fortunteller Baba Saga Tien Shinhan Saga King Piccolo Saga Piccolo Jr. Saga 9. Dragon Ball Z: Dead Zone (Movie) Garlic Jr. kidnaps Gohan, so Goku must rescue his son. 11. Dragon Ball Z (Episodes 1-86) Raditz Saga Vegeta Saga Namek Saga Captain Ginyu Saga Start of Frieza Saga 12. Dragon Ball Z: Bardock – The Father of Goku (Special) A prequel showing the final days of the planet Vegeta before Frieza destroyed it, focusing on Goku's father, Bardock. 13. Dragon Ball Z (Episodes 87-107) Rest of Frieza Saga 14. Dragon Ball Z: The World's Strongest (Movie) Goku and his friends must defeat an evil scientist who kidnaps Bulma, but when Gohan shows his incredible power, the scientist tries to steal his body! 15. Dragon Ball Z: The Tree of Might (Movie) We have pirates now! A Sayian pirate called Turles and his crew attempt to conquer the Earth by planting a magical tree that can absorb all life on the planet and leave it a desolated wasteland. 16. Dragon Ball Z: Lord Slug (Movie) What if Dragon Ball was Michael Bay's Armageddon? This time, Earth is threatened by a massive asteroid on a collision course towards Earth. While Krillin and Goku head out to stop it, a Namekian conqueror tries to use the Dragon Balls to take over Earth. 17. Dragon Ball Z (Episodes 108-123) Garlic Jr. Saga Start of Trunks Saga 18. Dragon Ball Z: The History of Trunks (Special) A special depicting the post-apocalyptic future that Trunks comes from, and how the sword-wielding teenager went back in time to prevent his future from existing. 19. Dragon Ball Z (Episodes 124-125) Rest of Trunks Saga 20. Dragon Ball Z: Cooler's Revenge (Movie) Goku and his friends go on a camping trip after the defeat of Frieza, but their celebrations are interrupted when the alien conqueror's older brother comes looking for revenge. 21. Dragon Ball Z (Episodes 126-139) Androids Saga 22. Dragon Ball Z: Super Android 13 (Movie) New terrifying murder androids, 13, 14, and 15 are activated after Android 17 and 18 murder Dr. Gero. Now, Goku and the Z Fighters must deal with them. 23. Dragon Ball Z (Episodes 140-165) Imperfect Cell Saga Perfect Cell Saga 24. Dragon Ball Z: The Return of Cooler Cooler is back, and now he's a robot! After enslaving the people of New Namek, Cooler arrives on Earth with an army of robots. Making matters worse, the world-be conqueror claims to have killed Goku. 25. Dragon Ball Z: Broly – The Legendary Super Saiyan The Z Fighters are invited to the planet New Vegeta. There, they catch wind of a legendary Super Saiyan hellbent on destroying the universe. 26. Dragon Ball Z (Episodes 166-194) Cell Games Saga 27. Dragon Ball Z: Bojack Unbound Gohan finally gets the spotlight! The demon Bojack is finally free, and he decides to host the biggest martial arts tournament in the galaxy, and Gohan is the only one capable of saving the Earth. 28. Dragon Ball Z (Episodes 195-209) Other World Saga Great Saiyaman Saga 29. Dragon Ball Z: Broly – Second Coming (Movie) Broly is back, awakened by Goten's crying (yes, this actually happened). This movie is memorable for having a Father-Sons Kamehameha with Gohan, Goten and Goku's spirit. 30. Dragon Ball Z: Bio-Broly (Movie) Yes, Broly is still somehow around, and he returns yet again as a clone. Goten, Trunks, and best boy Krillin have to stop him. 31. Dragon Ball Z (Episodes 210-287) World Tournament Saga Babidi Saga Majin Buu Saga Fusion Saga Kid Buu Saga 32. Dragon Ball Z: Fusion Reborn (Movie) A fever dream of a movie, featuring villains long dead. Worth watching because of Vegeta and Goku's fusion form, but generally part of its own timeline. 33. Dragon Ball Z: Wrath of the Dragon (Movie) The gang fights a kaiju in this movie, which has some of the best music in the franchise. 34. Dragon Ball GT (Episodes 1-64) The not-quite canon Dragon Ball series originally aired after Dragon Ball Z and is generally considered to be a part of its own timeline. Emperor Pilaf uses the Black Star Dragon Ball to turn Goku into a child. 35. Dragon Ball Daima (Episodes 1-20) The most recent Dragon Ball series follows Goku and friends who have been turned into children and must traverse the Demon Realm to become adults again. 36. Dragon Ball Super (Episodes 1-27) The next two Dragon Ball Z movies (Battle of the Gods and Resurrection F) and the first two sagas of Dragon Ball Super cover the same general storylines, but with some key differences. The Dragon Ball Super sagas are considered canon, but it's worth checking both out. Gods of Destruction Beerus Saga Golden Frieza Arc 37. Dragon Ball Z: Battle of the Gods (Movie) This is the movie where Goku fights a literal god, and all arguments about who can and can't defeat Goku become forever pointless. 39. Dragon Ball Z: Resurrection F (Movie) No one ever dies in Dragon Ball, so of course Frieza comes back to life and swears revenge on Goku. That's it. That's the movie. Oh, and Vegeta gets a cool new power. 40. Dragon Ball Super (Episodes 28-131) Universe 6 Saga Copy Vegeta Saga "Future" Trunks Saga Universe Survival Saga 41. Dragon Ball Super: Broly (Movie) The film tells the story of Broly and his history with Goku, Raditz and Vegeta. In the present, Broly returns yet again to wreak havoc, and it is up to Goku and Vegeta to literally combine forces to stop him. 42. Dragon Ball Super: Super Hero (Movie) The best father-son duo, Piccolo and Gohan, finally get the spotlight! We also get the triumphant return of the Red Ribbon Army, who create androids to take over the world. 43. Dragon Ball Z (Episodes 289-291) Peaceful World Saga I wouldn't recommend splitting up Dragon Ball Z like this on your first watch, but the original ending saga technically takes place 10 years after the defeat of Majin Buu. At the very least, it may be worth coming back to these final episodes after watching Dragon Ball Super. What's Next for Dragon Ball It’s been 8 years, but Dragon Ball Super is finally set to return. At a recent Dragon Ball 40th anniversary event , it was announced that Dragon Ball Super will return with The Galactic Patrol, an anime adaptation of the Galactic Patrol Prisoner Arc. It will follow Goku and Vegeta teaming up to capture the nefarious Moro. Though we don’t know when The Galactic Patrol will premiere, we also got the announcement that Dragon Ball Super: Beerus – a remake of the first arc of Dragon Ball Super – is set to be released in Fall 2026. Outside of animation, we recently learned that we'll be getting Dragon Ball-themed LEGO sets . The franchise also released a collaboration with Converse earlier this year.
